fixes.explanation: That's them. Elijah and Moses appeared before the three disciples, talking with Jesus (Mark 9:4). The text doesn't tell us what they said. Three disciples watching this, and I bet it was a lot to take in.

Abraham and David are two big names, so I see why they came to mind. But Mark says it was Elijah and Moses who appeared and talked with Jesus (Mark 9:4). Mark doesn't mention Abraham or David on that mountain.
Samuel and Isaiah are two more big names, and it's a fine guess. Still, Mark names Elijah and Moses as the two who appeared (Mark 9:4). They were the ones talking with Jesus up there.

Right, because the three shelters weren't for the disciples. Peter said, "Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." (Mark 9:5) So the shelters were for Jesus, Moses and Elijah. Not one of the three had Peter's name on it.

Yes. Mark says, "…they were all so terrified that Peter did not know what else to say." (Mark 9:6) They weren't just nervous, they were all terrified. Mark puts that right after Jesus was transfigured and Moses and Elijah appeared with Him.

Proud is a fun guess, but it's not what the text says. Mark says, "…they were all so terrified that Peter did not know what else to say." (Mark 9:6) Terrified is the word Mark uses, and it covers all three of them.

Elijah was right there on the mountain, so it's a fair guess. But the voice from the cloud says, "This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!" (Mark 9:7) Then, when the disciples looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus (Mark 9:8). So Jesus is the One the voice names.

Not quite. Mark says that when they looked around, "…they saw no one with them except Jesus." (Mark 9:8) Moses and Elijah weren't standing there anymore. Mark says it happened suddenly, and that's all the text gives us.

Yes. Jesus told them "…not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead." (Mark 9:9) Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). So Jesus put a limit on the silence, and the limit was His rising from the dead.

That would've been a quick announcement, but Jesus said not to tell anyone (Mark 9:9). The text doesn't make an exception for the other disciples. The instruction was to wait until the Son of Man had risen from the dead, and the three kept the matter to themselves (Mark 9:10).
